body.statement:
Every member of the intensity-optimized clipped-ramp family satisfies the declared fixed-outcome, outcome-boundedness, predictable-randomization, propensity-range, predictable-regression, intensity-profile, and residual-profile conditions. The intensity obeys
\[
 \bar q_\star(0)=c,\qquad c/2\leq\bar q_\star(u)\leq c\leq K,
 \qquad |\bar q_\star(u)-\bar q_\star(v)|\leq L_q|u-v|.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), the propensity cap is inactive at every time after the profile cutoff, hence also at every time after both that cutoff and the late-ramp start; both profile discrepancies in \(G_n\) are zero, the early rare-arm term and its predictable quadratic variation are zero, and \(G_n=\Omega\). Consequently \(\bar q_\star\in\mathcal Q\), \(r^\sigma\in\mathcal R\), and the profile contract holds eventually with probability one.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(f(u)=c-L_qu\) and \(b=c/2\). Since the map \(x\mapsto\max\{x,b\}\) is nondecreasing and one-Lipschitz,
\[
 |\bar q_\star(u)-\bar q_\star(v)|
 =|\max\{f(u),b\}-\max\{f(v),b\}|
 \leq |f(u)-f(v)|=L_q|u-v|.
\]
Moreover \(\bar q_\star(0)=\max\{c,c/2\}=c\), and, for every \(u\in[0,1]\),
\[
 c/2\leq\bar q_\star(u)\leq c\leq K.
\]
These equations verify the anchor, bound, and Lipschitz conditions, so the definition of \(\mathcal Q\) gives \(\bar q_\star\in\mathcal Q\).

The positive-part map is one-Lipschitz, and truncation by \(M\) cannot increase distances. Hence
\[
 |g_{a_\star}(u)-g_{a_\star}(v)|\leq L_r|u-v|,
 \qquad 0\leq g_{a_\star}(u)\leq M\leq B.
\]
Therefore \(|r^\sigma(u)|\leq B\) and \(r^\sigma\) is \(L_r\)-Lipschitz; the definition of \(\mathcal R\) yields \(r^\sigma\in\mathcal R\). The displayed construction makes the potential outcomes fixed under randomization and gives \(|Y_{nt}^\sigma(a)|\leq M\). It also makes both regressions identically zero, hence predictable and bounded by the nonnegative constant \(M_m\). Since \(0<\bar q_\star(t/n)/t\) and \(0<\rho<1\),
\[
 0<e_{nt}=\min\{\rho,\bar q_\star(t/n)/t\}\leq\rho<1.
\]
The required conditional assignment equality holds by the construction of the sequential law.

It remains to verify the profile event rather than assume its eventual validity. Because \(n\varepsilon_n\to\infty\), for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil>c/\rho.
\]
For every \(t\geq\lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil\), the upper bound \(\bar q_\star\leq c\) then gives \(\bar q_\star(t/n)/t<\rho\), whence
\[
 t e_{nt}=\bar q_\star(t/n).
\]
Thus the propensity cap is inactive after the profile cutoff. In particular it is inactive after the maximum of that cutoff and \(\lfloor a_\star n\rfloor+1\). The construction also gives, for every \(t\),
\[
 r_{nt}(1)=Y_{nt}^\sigma(1)-m_{nt}(1)=r^\sigma(t/n),
\]
so the residual-profile discrepancy is zero.

Finally, since \(\varepsilon_n\to0\), eventually \(\varepsilon_n+1/n<a_\star\). If \(t<\lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil\), then
\[
 t/n<\lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil/n\leq\varepsilon_n+1/n<a_\star,
\]
and consequently \(r_{nt}(1)=0\). Every summand of \(S_{n,\mathrm{rare}}^{\mathrm{early}}\) is then zero, so that martingale and its predictable quadratic variation are both zero. All three components in the definition of \(G_n\) therefore hold on every assignment path for all sufficiently large \(n\). Thus \(G_n=\Omega\), and \(\Pr(G_n)=1\geq1-\kappa_n\) eventually.
